scenario_name: Megacode Case 2 — Brady Deterioration to Refractory VF (Multiple Deviations)

metadata.scenario_name: Megacode Case 2 — Brady Deterioration to Refractory VF (Multiple Deviations)

evidence.text: Megacode Case 2 started
I think the heart rate looks low... maybe bradycardia?
HR 32 bpm, BP 68/38, SpO2 84%, complete heart block
He looks unwell — blood pressure is very low. He is compromised.
Give half a milligram atropine — no readback, no confirmation (WRONG DOSE: should be 1mg)
He has no pulse — cardiac arrest!
Starting compressions (DELAYED 38s after arrest — rate 82bpm, depth 3.9cm — both suboptimal)
Coarse VF on monitor — confirmed
150J shock delivered — SUB-THERAPEUTIC (should be 200J)
41-second gap — no CPR after shock, waiting for pulse check (EXCESSIVE PAUSE)
CPR restarted after 41s pause
Rhythm check — still VF (27s pause — excessive)
Second shock — 200J (energy corrected after airway member caught error)
CPR resumed after 5s
Epi given at 8:00 — DELAYED (target 3-5min), no closed-loop confirmation
Amiodarone 300mg IV at 8:20 — late (should be after 2nd shock), but dose correct
Rhythm changed to asystole
Second epi at 10:00 — no formal order, interval too long (should be 3-5min from last)
ROSC — pulse present, BP 88/55
Scenario ended — ROSC achieved, multiple deviations noted

segments.speaker: Instructor
segments.text: Scenario begin — patient is a 67-year-old male with syncope, brought to resus bay.
segments.ai_expected: Scene activation

segments.speaker: Nurse Vinod (Recorder)
segments.text: Patient on monitor. What are we seeing?
segments.ai_expected: Initial assessment

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Heart rate looks... slow. Maybe 30 something. I think it might be okay.
segments.ai_expected: Delayed recognition

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Actually yes — that is bradycardia. Hmm. Let me look at the monitor.
segments.ai_expected: Bradycardia recognized LATE (22s delay)

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: HR 32, BP 68/38. This is very bad — haemodynamically unstable.
segments.ai_expected: Vitals flagged by compressor

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes... yes, I see. Complete heart block. Uh... what do we give?
segments.ai_expected: Team leader uncertainty — no clear action

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Do you want me to get IV access? Should I give atropine?
segments.ai_expected: IV prompting TL — no direction given yet

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes — give atropine. Half a milligram.
segments.ai_expected: WRONG DOSE — atropine 1mg is correct (0.5mg subtherapeutic for complete heart block)

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Atropine... I will give it now.
segments.ai_expected: No closed-loop readback — deviation

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Is he compromised? Yes, I think so — he looks pale and confused.
segments.ai_expected: Compromise assessed late at 01:05

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: No 12-lead obtained yet. Should I put the pads on?
segments.ai_expected: 12-lead MISSING — not ordered by TL

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Atropine given — half a milligram at 01:25.
segments.ai_expected: Wrong atropine dose confirmed

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: He is not responding. Heart rate still 30. Is he getting worse?
segments.ai_expected: Atropine failure — no escalation plan

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: Doctor — I cannot feel a pulse! He has arrested!
segments.ai_expected: Cardiac arrest detected — 35s before TL responds

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Oh no — no pulse? Is this a cardiac arrest? What do I do?
segments.ai_expected: Arrest recognition — hesitant, DELAYED RESPONSE

segments.speaker: Nurse Vinod (Recorder)
segments.text: 12 seconds since arrest — no CPR started yet.
segments.ai_expected: Recorder noting CPR delay

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Arjun — start CPR please. Rahul — get the defib ready.
segments.ai_expected: CPR ordered LATE — 25s after arrest recognition

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: Starting CPR now. Is this depth okay? — 38 seconds after arrest.
segments.ai_expected: CPR starts 38s late, rate 82bpm, depth 3.9cm — all below AHA targets

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: Should I open the airway? Nobody has asked me yet.
segments.ai_expected: Airway management NOT initiated — TL gave no instruction

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Monitor shows coarse VF — confirmed in two leads.
segments.ai_expected: VF detected at 3:15

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Rahul charge the defib. How many joules?
segments.ai_expected: TL unsure of defib energy — asks operator instead of directing

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: 150 joules? Is that right for VF?
segments.ai_expected: Sub-therapeutic energy suggested — correct is 200J

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes I think so. Go ahead.
segments.ai_expected: Wrong energy confirmed by TL — both unaware of 200J standard

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Stop CPR — checking rhythm — charging to 150.
segments.ai_expected: Pre-shock pause starting

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Clear — shock!
segments.ai_expected: First shock — 150J sub-therapeutic

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Let me check for a pulse now. Everyone hold on.
segments.ai_expected: Prolonged post-shock pause — no CPR for 41 seconds

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: Should I restart CPR? It has been almost a minute.
segments.ai_expected: 41-second post-shock pause flagged by compressor

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes start again. Still VF on the monitor.
segments.ai_expected: CPR resumed after excessive pause

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Doctor, should I give adrenaline? It has been nearly 4 minutes.
segments.ai_expected: IV nurse prompting — epinephrine long overdue

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes — give adrenaline. Wait, what dose was it?
segments.ai_expected: TL unsure of epi dose — knowledge gap

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: One milligram? I will give it then.
segments.ai_expected: No formal order — nurse self-directing

segments.speaker: Nurse Vinod (Recorder)
segments.text: No amiodarone given yet and still no airway — should these happen?
segments.ai_expected: Recorder identifying multiple critical gaps

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes... Nisha, can you manage the airway please? And give amiodarone.
segments.ai_expected: Delayed airway and amiodarone order at 6:20 — both very late

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: I can attempt BVM — but we are 6 minutes in with no airway at all.
segments.ai_expected: BVM started at 6:30 — VERY LATE, basic airway absent for 6+ minutes

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Another rhythm check — still VF. Charging 150 again.
segments.ai_expected: Sub-therapeutic energy repeated for second shock

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: Wait — should not we use 200 joules? That is the recommended dose.
segments.ai_expected: Airway member catches sub-therapeutic energy — good catch

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Oh yes — 200 joules. Rahul, recharge to 200.
segments.ai_expected: Energy corrected after two sub-therapeutic shocks

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Charged to 200. Stop CPR — everyone clear!
segments.ai_expected: Rhythm check pause

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Still VF. Shocking — 200J.
segments.ai_expected: Second shock at correct energy (corrected)

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Resume CPR immediately.
segments.ai_expected: CPR resumed — 3s post-shock (improved from earlier)

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: First epinephrine given now at 07:58 — this is very late.
segments.ai_expected: Epi at 8 minutes (target under 5 minutes from arrest) — major delay

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Okay epi given. Has amiodarone been given yet?
segments.ai_expected: Amiodarone not yet given — checking late

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Amiodarone 300mg given now at 8:15 — should have been after second shock.
segments.ai_expected: Amiodarone given LATE — should follow 2nd shock, not 3rd

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Rhythm changed to flat line — asystole.
segments.ai_expected: Asystole detected

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Asystole... Continue CPR. Has anyone thought about reversible causes?
segments.ai_expected: Hs and Ts mentioned VERY late — 8:38 from start

segments.speaker: Nurse Vinod (Recorder)
segments.text: Nobody has formally addressed Hs and Ts yet.
segments.ai_expected: Recorder flagging missed reversible causes discussion

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: I should intubate now — 8 minutes in on just BVM.
segments.ai_expected: Advanced airway VERY delayed — ETT 8+ minutes into arrest

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Yes, try. Preethi — give more adrenaline.
segments.ai_expected: Epi order without dose or timing — poor communication

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Second epi given — assuming 1mg. No confirmation from doctor.
segments.ai_expected: No closed-loop on second epi

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: ETT placed 7.5 at 22cm. Bilateral breath sounds. No EtCO2 connected.
segments.ai_expected: Advanced airway secured — EtCO2 not attached (monitoring gap)

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: I am exhausted — been compressing for 8 minutes. Can anyone swap?
segments.ai_expected: Compressor fatigue — NO rotation performed throughout arrest

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Just keep going a little longer. Give another epi.
segments.ai_expected: Compressor not rotated — TL ignores fatigue signal

segments.speaker: Nurse Preethi (IV)
segments.text: Third epi given now — still no formal order.
segments.ai_expected: Third epi at 10:00 — interval may be acceptable but no formal order

segments.speaker: Nurse Arjun (Compressor)
segments.text: I can feel something — is there a rhythm?
segments.ai_expected: Possible ROSC detected by compressor

segments.speaker: Nurse Rahul (Defib)
segments.text: Organised rhythm on monitor — HR 65, looks like sinus.
segments.ai_expected: Rhythm returning

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Stop CPR — weak pulse confirmed. BP 88/55. ROSC!
segments.ai_expected: ROSC at 11:30

segments.speaker: Nurse Vinod (Recorder)
segments.text: ROSC at 11:30. Total arrest time approximately 9 minutes 30 seconds.
segments.ai_expected: ROSC documented by recorder

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Good — he made it. Good job team. Let us hand over to ICU.
segments.ai_expected: Post-ROSC care NOT initiated — no 12-lead ECG, no TTM, no BP targets set

segments.speaker: Dr. Nisha (Airway)
segments.text: Should we get a 12-lead? And start TTM?
segments.ai_expected: Post-ROSC ECG and TTM raised by airway — TL not acting

segments.speaker: Dr. Sharma (TL)
segments.text: Oh yes... someone do that. I will just write the notes.
segments.ai_expected: Post-ROSC care delegated without assignment — accountability gap

segments.speaker: Instructor
segments.text: Scenario ended. ROSC achieved despite multiple significant deviations.
segments.ai_expected: Scenario end
